data.title: Novartis: Unchanged $113 Price Target Reflects Patent-Expiry Risks and Uncertain Growth Replacements
data.description:
Novartis AG, the Healthcare sector company, was revisited by a Wall Street analyst today. Analyst James Quigley from Goldman Sachs maintained a Sell rating on the stock and has a CHF113.00 price target.

James Quigley’s rating is based on several factors, especially the risk that upcoming patent expirations for Entresto, Cosentyx, Kesimpta, and Kisqali will pressure Novartis AG’s growth late this decade and into the 2030s. Although management raised its 2026–31 revenue outlook and reiterated mid-single-digit growth beyond 2030, investors appear unconvinced that the company can replace lost franchise sales quickly enough.
Quigley also believes the longer-term ambition depends on above-average clinical success, indication expansion, or additional late-stage acquisitions, none of which is assured. Potential contributions from Rhapsido, ianalumab, and artificial intelligence may be meaningful, but their benefits are expected to take time to emerge; accordingly, the price target remains unchanged at $113, implying downside from the current share price.

In another report released on November 10, Deutsche Bank also maintained a Sell rating on the stock with a CHF115.00 price target.
